questions.passage: Hajun wanted to join the school's soccer club. ① Many of his classmates were already members, and they kept telling him how great it was. ② Without thinking much, he signed up. ③ However, after a few weeks, he realized that he didn't really enjoy soccer. ④ He had joined simply because everyone else was doing it.
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"He felt a strong pull to be part of the group."

det.korean: 많은 친구들이 이미 회원이고 좋다고 말하는 상황 뒤, 그룹에 속하고 싶은 강한 끌림을 느꼈다는 문장이 와야 자연스럽다. 그 후 별 생각 없이 가입했다는 내용으로 이어진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: "classmates were already members" + "telling him how great" 직후 → 그룹에 속하고 싶은 끌림 → "Without thinking much, he signed up"으로 자연스러운 흐름
❌ ①: 아직 상황 설명 전
❌ ②: 친구들의 영향 설명 전
❌ ④: 이미 후회 단계 → 끌림은 시간 역전
det.tip: 인과 흐름: 친구들의 권유 → 소속감 욕구(끌림) → 가입 행동

questions.passage: Yubin had an important English exam coming up. ① She was worried about getting a bad grade. ② So, instead of studying hard, she spent the night before the exam watching TV. ③ The next day, she got a low score. ④ She told herself, "I didn't fail because I'm bad at English. I failed because I didn't study."
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"To protect herself from the possibility of failure, she created an excuse in advance."

det.korean: 시험 걱정 뒤, 실패 가능성으로부터 자신을 보호하기 위해 미리 핑계를 만들었다는 내용이 와야 한다. 그 후 공부 대신 TV를 본 행동으로 이어진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ②: 시험 걱정 직후 → 미리 핑계 만들기 → TV 시청(핑계 실행)으로 자연스러운 흐름
❌ ①: 아직 걱정 언급 전
❌ ③: 이미 행동 완료 후
❌ ④: 결과 발생 후 → 미리 핑계가 아님
det.tip: self-handicapping 순서: 걱정 → 핑계 준비 → 핑계 행동 실행 → 결과

questions.passage: The bandwagon effect and self-handicapping are common psychological patterns. However, being aware of these tendencies can help us __________________________________________. By understanding why we act the way we do, we can make better choices.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.

negative / ourselves / about / overcome / feelings

det.korean: "overcome negative feelings about ourselves" → 우리 자신에 대한 부정적인 감정을 극복하다.
det.analysis:
overcome(동사) + negative feelings(목적어) + about ourselves(전치사구)
help us 뒤에 동사원형이 와야 함 → overcome
det.tip: help + 목적어 + 동사원형: help us overcome ~

questions.passage: The bandwagon effect is the tendency to follow __________________________________________ rather than making your own decision. People often do things just because many other people are doing them.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.

doing / what / are / others

det.korean: "what others are doing" → 다른 사람들이 하고 있는 것. 간접의문문 어순.
det.analysis:
what(관계대명사) + others(주어) + are doing(동사)
follow의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절
det.tip: 간접의문문/명사절: what + S + V (의문사 + 주어 + 동사 순서)

questions.passage: Hajun wanted to join the school's soccer club. Many of his classmates were already members, and they kept ①<u>telling</u> him how great it was. He felt a strong pull to be part of the group, so without ②<u>thinking</u> much, he signed up. However, after a few weeks, he ③<u>was realized</u> that he didn't really enjoy soccer. He had ④<u>joined</u> simply because everyone else ⑤<u>was doing</u> it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ was realized → realized: realize는 타동사로 "깨달았다"는 뜻이며, 능동태로 써야 한다. 수동태 was realized는 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ was realized: realize(깨닫다)는 능동태 → realized
✅ ① telling: keep ~ing(계속 ~하다) → 올바름
✅ ② thinking: without ~ing(~하지 않고) → 올바름
✅ ④ joined: had joined(과거완료) → 올바름
✅ ⑤ was doing: 과거진행형 → 올바름
det.tip: realize는 능동태 동사: "He realized that ~" (그는 ~을 깨달았다)

questions.passage: Yubin had an important English exam coming up. She was worried about getting a bad grade. __________ herself from the possibility of failure, she created an excuse in advance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "자신을 보호하기 위해" → 목적을 나타내는 to protect(to부정사의 부사적 용법)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ to protect: 목적의 부사적 용법 → "~하기 위해"
❌ ① protect: 원형 불가 (접속사 없음)
❌ ② protected: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 동사 연결 불가
❌ ④ protecting: 분사구문 가능하나, 목적("~하기 위해")의 의미가 더 적절
det.tip: To + 동사원형(목적): ~하기 위해 → To protect herself from ~

questions.passage: In a famous experiment, Zajonc showed participants a series of unfamiliar images. The more frequently people were __________ to something, the more they tended to develop a preference for it. This became known as the Mere Exposure Effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "사람들이 무언가에 노출될수록" → 수동태 were exposed to가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① exposed: were exposed to(~에 노출되다) → 수동태
❌ ② exposing: 능동 → 사람들이 노출하는 게 아님
❌ ③ to expose: 부정사 → 구조 불일치
❌ ④ having exposed: 완료분사 능동 → 부적절
det.tip: be exposed to ~ = ~에 노출되다 (수동태) / expose A to B = A를 B에 노출시키다 (능동태)

questions.passage: Hajun wanted to join the school's soccer club. Many of his classmates were already members, and they kept telling him how ①<u>great</u> it was. Without thinking much, he signed up. However, after a few weeks, he realized that he didn't really ②<u>enjoy</u> soccer. He had joined simply because everyone else was doing it. This is called the bandwagon effect — the ③<u>reluctance</u> to follow what others are doing rather than making your own decision.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 편승 효과는 다른 사람이 하는 것을 따르려는 "경향(tendency)"이다. ③ reluctance(꺼림)는 반대 의미로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ reluctance(꺼림/주저): 원래 tendency(경향) → 따르려는 경향이지 꺼림이 아님
✅ ① great(좋은): 친구들이 좋다고 말함 → 적절
✅ ② enjoy(즐기다): 축구를 즐기지 못함 → 적절
✅ ④⑤ 해당 없음
det.tip: tendency(경향) ↔ reluctance(꺼림) — bandwagon effect는 따르려는 "경향"

questions.passage: Self-handicapping is a strategy where people create obstacles for themselves before a challenging situation. By doing so, if they fail, they have a ready-made excuse. The real purpose of this behavior is to __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 셀프 핸디캐핑의 진짜 목적은 실패 시 핑계를 만들어 자존감을 보호하는 것(protect their self-esteem)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② protect their self-esteem: 실패해도 능력 탓이 아닌 핑계 탓 → 자존감 보호
❌ ① succeed without effort: 목적이 성공이 아님
❌ ③ improve their study habits: 오히려 공부를 안 함
❌ ④ impress their classmates: 인상을 주는 것과 무관
det.tip: self-handicapping의 핵심: 실패 시 핑계 → 자존감(self-esteem) 보호

questions.passage: When the Eiffel Tower was first built in 1889, many Parisians hated it. However, as time passed and people saw it every day, their feelings changed. They began to like it. Zajonc's experiment explains this: repeated exposure creates __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 반복 노출이 만들어내는 것은 친숙함(familiarity)이다. 에펠탑을 매일 보면서 친숙해져 좋아하게 됨.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ familiarity(친숙함): 반복 노출 → 친숙 → 선호 (Mere Exposure Effect)
❌ ① fear: 반복 노출의 결과가 아님
❌ ② anger: 초기 반응이었으나 변화됨
❌ ③ confusion: 문맥과 무관
det.tip: Mere Exposure Effect: 반복 노출 → 친숙함(familiarity) → 선호(preference)

questions.passage: The bandwagon effect and self-handicapping are common __________ (psychology) patterns that influence our daily decisions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: psychology(명사) → psychological(형용사): 명사 patterns를 수식하는 형용사 필요. "심리적인 패턴"
det.analysis:
psychology(명사) → psychological(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 patterns(명사)를 수식하는 형용사 필요
psychological patterns = 심리적 패턴
det.tip: psychology → psychological / biology → biological — 명사 → -ical 형용사화

questions.passage: In a famous experiment, Zajonc showed participants a series of __________ (familiar) images. After repeated exposure, participants began to prefer the images they had seen more often.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: familiar(형용사) → unfamiliar(형용사): 처음 보여준 이미지는 "낯선" 것이어야 한다. 접두사 un- 추가.
det.analysis:
familiar(익숙한) → unfamiliar(낯선)
실험에서 처음 보여준 이미지는 낯선 것 → 반복 노출 후 선호하게 됨
det.tip: familiar(익숙한) ↔ unfamiliar(낯선) — un- 접두사로 반의어

questions.passage: Hajun joined the soccer club simply because everyone else was doing it. He didn't really think about whether he liked soccer or not. This tendency to follow what others are doing is called the bandwagon effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 다른 사람들이 하는 것을 따르는 경향을 가리키는 용어를 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "This tendency to follow what others are doing is called the bandwagon effect" → 편승 효과
det.analysis:
다른 사람을 따르는 경향 = bandwagon effect
2단어 답 = bandwagon effect
det.tip: bandwagon effect = 편승 효과 — 다수가 하는 것을 따르는 심리적 경향

questions.passage: Zajonc's experiment showed that the more frequently people were exposed to something, the more they tended to develop a preference for it. This phenomenon is known as the Mere Exposure Effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 반복 노출이 선호도를 높이는 현상의 이름을 본문에서 3단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "This phenomenon is known as the Mere Exposure Effect" → 단순 노출 효과
det.analysis:
반복 노출 → 선호도 증가 현상 = Mere Exposure Effect
3단어 답 = Mere Exposure Effect
det.tip: Mere Exposure Effect = 단순 노출 효과 — 자주 접할수록 좋아하게 되는 현상

questions.passage: Hajun wanted to join the school's soccer club. Many of his classmates were already members, and they kept telling him how great it was. Without thinking much, he signed up. However, after a few weeks, he realized that he didn't really enjoy soccer. He had joined simply because everyone else was doing it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "Many of his classmates were already members, and they kept telling him how great it was" → 친구들의 영향으로 가입.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 친구들의 영향: "classmates kept telling him" + "everyone else was doing it" → 일치
❌ ① 축구를 좋아함: "didn't really enjoy soccer" → 불일치
❌ ③ 부모님 권유: 언급 없음
❌ ④ 코치 제안: 언급 없음
det.tip: 핵심: "joined simply because everyone else was doing it" = 친구들의 영향

questions.passage: When the Eiffel Tower was first built in 1889, many Parisians hated it. However, as time passed and people saw it every day, their feelings changed. They began to like it. Zajonc's experiment explains this phenomenon: the more frequently people were exposed to something, the more they developed a preference for it. This is called the Mere Exposure Effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: "many Parisians hated it" → 처음에 싫어했으므로, "건설 당시부터 자랑이었다"는 불일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 건설 당시부터 자랑: "many Parisians hated it" → 처음에 싫어함 → 불일치
✅ ① 환영받지 못함: "hated it" → 일치
✅ ② Zajonc 연구: 반복 노출과 선호 관계 → 일치
✅ ④ 단순 노출 효과: "exposed → preference" → 일치
det.tip: "hated it"(싫어함) ≠ "자랑이었다" — 에펠탑은 처음에 비판받았다

ch: 에펠탑은 처음에 파리 시민들에게 환영받지 못했다.
Zajonc은 반복 노출과 선호의 관계를 연구했다.
단순 노출 효과는 익숙해질수록 선호도가 높아지는 현상이다.

questions.passage: The bandwagon effect and self-handicapping are common psychological patterns. However, being aware of these tendencies can help us overcome negative feelings about ourselves. By understanding why we act the way we do, we can make better choices.
questions.stem: 이 글 전체의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 편승 효과와 셀프 핸디캐핑이라는 심리적 패턴을 이해하면 더 나은 선택을 할 수 있다 → 행동에 영향을 미치는 심리적 패턴의 이해
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 심리적 패턴의 이해: "psychological patterns" + "understanding why we act" → 정확히 일치
❌ ① 시험 공부: 부분적 소재일 뿐
❌ ② 친구 관계: 본문 주제 아님
❌ ④ 스포츠 클럽: 예시일 뿐
det.tip: 글의 주제 = 심리적 패턴(bandwagon effect, self-handicapping)을 이해하고 극복하기

ch: 행동에 영향을 미치는 심리적 패턴의 이해

questions.passage: Yubin had an important English exam coming up. She was worried about getting a bad grade. To protect herself from the possibility of failure, she created an excuse in advance. So, instead of studying hard, she spent the night before the exam watching TV.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Yubin did not study hard for her English exam."

det.korean: "instead of studying hard, she spent the night before the exam watching TV" → 열심히 공부하지 않았다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "instead of studying hard" + "watching TV" → 공부하지 않음
det.tip: instead of ~ing = ~하는 대신에 → 공부 대신 TV 시청

questions.passage: Hajun wanted to join the school's soccer club. Many of his classmates were already members, and they kept telling him how great it was. Without thinking much, he signed up. However, after a few weeks, he realized that he didn't really enjoy soccer.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Hajun carefully considered his decision before joining the soccer club."

det.korean: 본문: "Without thinking much, he signed up" → 별 생각 없이 가입했으므로 "신중하게 고려했다"는 False.
det.analysis: ❌ False: "Without thinking much"(별 생각 없이) ≠ "carefully considered"(신중하게 고려)
det.tip: without thinking much(별 생각 없이) ↔ carefully considered(신중하게 고려) — 반대 의미

questions.passage: The next day, she got a low score. She told herself, "I didn't fail because I'm bad at English. I failed because I didn't study." This way, she could blame her poor performance on a lack of effort rather than a lack of ability. This behavior is called self-handicapping.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Self-handicapping allows a person to attribute failure to external factors rather than personal ability."

det.korean: "blame her poor performance on a lack of effort rather than a lack of ability" → 실패를 능력 부족이 아닌 노력 부족(외적 요인)으로 돌림. → True
det.analysis:
✅ True: "lack of effort rather than lack of ability" → 능력이 아닌 외적 요인(노력 부족)으로 귀인
attribute failure to external factors = blame on lack of effort
det.tip: self-handicapping의 핵심: 실패 원인을 능력(ability)이 아닌 외적 요인(effort)으로 돌리기
